findings.claim: §6.4's promise that `pane.setSettings()` "must never land in (or be lost with) a transient" is satisfied only literally: the selection transient is seeded with a FULL value snapshot of the anchor's settings, so every host write to the local tier (and to any host layer) is invisible for the whole episode and then pops into effect on deselect — with no `settings` event to tell the host it happened.
findings.evidence: `useSeedGroupOnFormation` (renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:112-128) clears the group layer and publishes `snapshot()` — and the snapshot is not a diff, it is the pane's complete effective set: `encoding, tonemapGamma, peak, exposureEV, offset, reduce, colorMin/colorMax, compareMode, diffKernel, splitPosition` (renderers/GpuImagePane.tsx:885-920). Merge is `Object.assign({}, ...layers)` bottom→top (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:212-224), and v2's order is `[local, ...host layers, ...transients]` (§6.4), so the transient shadows every one of those keys. Failing scenario: a card holds a persisted `exposureEV: 2`; the user shift-selects two panes; the card calls `pane.setSettings({exposureEV: 5})`; nothing renders differently, `pane.on("settings")` never fires (§6.4 says it fires "once per resolved-value change" and the resolved value did not change), and 30 s later when the user unselects, the pane jumps to EV 5 with no host action.
findings.proposal: State the shadowing explicitly and give the host a signal: either (a) emit a `settings` event carrying both `resolved` and `pending` (a host write shadowed by a live transient), or (b) make the formation seed write only the keys that differ from each member's own resolved value (a diff seed), which also fixes the §13-Q2 `episodeEnd` payload problem, or (c) forbid a transient from shadowing a key written into a lower tier *after* the transient was pushed (last-writer-wins across tiers for host writes).

findings.claim: The three-tier read order and the gesture write-routing rule contradict each other: a host layer pushed WITHOUT `gestureSink` reads above the local tier but gestures route below it, so any key that layer sets becomes a dead control — the user picks a colormap / drags exposure and the pane does not change and the menu snaps back.
findings.evidence: §6.4 read order is `[local, ...host layers, ...transients]` with top shadowing; §6.4 routing says gestures go to "the topmost transient if one is live … otherwise the host layer marked gestureSink … otherwise the local tier". Today the invariant is the opposite and is deliberate: `publishToSettingsStack` writes the TOP layer only, so a gesture always wins (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:161-163, 183-190; renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:18-21). Failing scenario: ScalarPlotCard pushes a persistence layer holding `{encoding: "turbo"}` (not a sink, because the card only wants to seed). With no selection live, the user opens the Display menu and picks `aces`: `setEncoding`→`publishSettings({encoding})` lands in local, is shadowed by the host layer, `getSettings()` still resolves `turbo`, and the menu value (derived from the store, display-encoding.ts:368-380) reverts. The spec offers `gestureSink` as the fix, but §6.4 also says layers are shareable across panes — marking a shared layer as the sink makes one pane's drag silently move every pane sharing it, which is exactly the mirroring the user restricted to selections.
findings.proposal: Pick one: either host layers read BELOW local (seed semantics — `[host layers, local, ...transients]`, gestures keep writing local and always win), or keep host-above-local but require a per-pane sink and make a non-sink host layer's keys visibly read-only (disable the control and say so in `getPaneCapabilities`) instead of silently swallowing the gesture. Also state whether a shared layer may be a sink for more than one pane.

findings.claim: §6.5's freshness model cannot reach the panes through the cache §6.2 leaves in front of it: the resolve cache is append-only with no invalidation, and the pane's lookup key is descriptor-derived while freshness is `contentKey`-derived — a value only known AFTER the fetch. Consequently a Tier-2 `onInvalidate` → re-`get` → new `contentKey` never changes what the pane renders, and a failed first resolve is poisoned for the page lifetime, contradicting LD4's "retries on the NEXT invalidation or an explicit `m.refresh()`".
findings.evidence: `resolveCached` returns the memoized entry forever and has no delete/invalidate export (resolve-cache.ts:82-101); the only reset is `__resetResolveCacheForTest` (:113-118). On failure the entry keeps a rejected `promise` and no `data`, so every later call takes the `existing?.promise` branch and re-throws the same error — `run` is never re-invoked. §6.5 explicitly keeps this layer ("The identity-keyed resolve cache remains for descriptor-node resolution and gains release hooks … the RefStore sits behind it") and §6.2 only makes its keys content-derived; release ≠ invalidate. Failing scenario A: a pane on `track://run7/loss@latest`; the adapter's `subscribe` fires, RefStore re-gets, contentKey changes step 100→200 — the descriptor and hence the resolve key are unchanged, `peekResolved(key)` still returns step 100, and the dashboard renders a permanently frozen frame while `status` claims `ready`. Failing scenario B: the first `get` fails on a flaky connection; `m.refresh(ref)` re-fetches into the RefStore, but the pane still reads the poisoned resolve entry and stays `error` forever.
findings.proposal: Either put the RefStore in FRONT (panes subscribe to `(ref, version)` and the resolve cache is keyed by `contentKey`, resolved after the fetch — which makes a versioned key legal), or add explicit `invalidateResolved(key)` / `dropResolveError(key)` to §6.2's M0d and require every RefStore invalidation and every `refresh()` to call it. Also specify that an errored entry is dropped rather than cached, so a retry actually re-runs `run`.

findings.claim: §6.2's "content-derived resolve keys (dataspec hash / runtime hash / src ref)" does not deliver its stated benefit for the primary host path: runtime hashes are minted fresh per registration, not content-addressed, so every `update()` on a JS-authored handle misses the cache and re-resolves + re-uploads every leaf even when the data object is identical.
findings.evidence: viewport/runtime-store.ts:117-126: `mintRuntimeHash` — "Uniqueness — not content-addressing — is all that's needed: JS data rides by reference, so a fresh id per registration is correct". A host doing Tier-1 live updates re-runs the builder (`cairnPlot.image(f32, …)`) to author `h2`; even if `f32` is the very same `Float32Array`, the builder registers it under a new `runtime:<n>-<rand>`, so the derived resolve key differs from generation N's and §6.5's "cheap for unchanged leaves" / §6.2's "re-uses the cached resolution and GPU upload" both fail. Secondary leak: `objectUrlCache` (runtime-store.ts:92-96) mints one `blob:` URL per hash and never revokes, so §7's leak gate ("mount → update ×100 → unmount → assert stores empty") accumulates 100 live object URLs that no acquire/release pair covers.
findings.proposal: Make M0d specify how a runtime entry becomes content-identified — either hash the buffer, or key on the buffer's object identity (WeakMap → stable hash) so re-registering the same array returns the existing hash. Add `objectUrlCache` revocation to the disposal invariants and to the leak test's assertions.

findings.claim: Expressing HOME as `{clear}` operations silently weakens the recorded ruling "HOME = the clicked pane's defaults for the whole group": a `clear` in a shared group layer resolves per-pane to THAT pane's descriptor default, so members with different authored seeds diverge instead of converging on the clicked pane.
findings.evidence: §6.4 defines `layer.clear(keys)` as "hide lower tiers' value; fall back to descriptor default", then says HOME's write "is expressed as `{clear}` operations for keys that equal descriptor defaults". Today HOME on a store-backed pane is a VALUE write of that pane's own seeds — display-encoding.ts:418-425: "On a controlled surface HOME is a STORE write (the pane publishes the defaults)", and the seed is computed from that pane's props (`seedFor` → `propColormap`/`propTonemap`, :336-346). Failing scenario: pane A authored `tonemap:"aces"`, pane B authored nothing (default `srgb`), both selected, user double-clicks A. Today both show ACES. With HOME emitting `clear("encoding")` into the group layer, A resolves ACES and B resolves sRGB — the group no longer mirrors the clicked pane. The one key where the clear-mapping genuinely holds is `infoPanel`, whose default is computed rather than authored (image-settings-sync.ts:80-83); v2 generalizes from that single case.
findings.proposal: Keep HOME a value write of the clicked pane's resolved defaults (the existing behavior) and drop the clear-optimization, or restrict `clear` to keys whose default is pane-independent and enumerate them. If clears are kept, §13-Q1 must also state what HOME means for a group whose members have different authored seeds — that is a second user ruling, not an implementation detail.

findings.claim: §6.7's `enumerateOptions(kind, field)` / `getPaneCapabilities(kind)` are keyed by pane KIND, but the real option sets are per-pane (channel arity, surface mode, the pane's own curve set, and for compare the light/scalar face). A host menu built from these offers ids that the pane will accept, store, and silently ignore.
findings.evidence: renderers/display-encoding.ts:100-120 `resolveDisplayEncodingIds({mode: "sdr"|"arity", arity, curveSet})` — `normal` only at arity 3, luts filtered by declared arities, curves filtered by the pane's `curveSet`; compare panes offer curves XOR luts by mode (:180-200). And applicability is deliberately a RENDER decision, never a sync/store decision (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:10-15, "a value that doesn't apply … is stored and simply doesn't alter that render"). Failing scenario: a card header renders `enumerateOptions("image", "encoding")`, the user picks `normal` on a scalar (k=1) pane, `setSettings({encoding:"normal"})` succeeds, `getSettings()` echoes `normal`, `pane.on("settings")` fires, and the image does not change — with no error and nothing in the API that could have told the host the id was inapplicable.
findings.proposal: Move the enumeration onto the Pane (`pane.options(field)` / `pane.capabilities()`, recomputed on content change and surfaced via a `capabilities` event), keeping the kind-level function only as the static superset and documenting it as such. Alternatively add an `applicable: boolean` flag per `OptionDescriptor` and require a pane argument.

findings.claim: §6.2's "Lazy/offscreen panes are included as fully functional Pane objects — settings and events work" contradicts how laziness is implemented: `LazyGate` gates MOUNTING, not just GPU work, so an offscreen leaf has no React subtree, no settings hook, no resolve in flight, and no state that `status` can honestly report; and §7's PERF-5 screenshot-restore and PERF-8 rootMargin are written against the wrong observer.
findings.evidence: lazy-mount.ts:1-19 — "`LazyGate` (plot-node.tsx) gates leaf/compare mounting behind a viewport `IntersectionObserver` so a pane only does its work as it nears the viewport"; the settings subscription lives inside the mounted pane (`useViewportSettings`, use-synced-image-settings.ts:72-104) and the encoding seed needs the resolved source's arity (display-encoding.ts:336-348), which does not exist before mount. `PaneStatus` is `"loading"|"ready"|"error"|"stale"` with no "not mounted" member, so a dashboard sees below-the-fold panes as permanently `loading`. PERF-5's "restores the pane" is the pool's park/restore path (engine/pool.ts:1-45), which only applies to panes that were mounted and parked — a never-mounted lazy pane has no `PaneHandle` to restore. PERF-8 says "the pane IntersectionObserver gains a rootMargin", but the lazy-mount observer already has one (`LAZY_ROOT_MARGIN = "600px 0px"`, lazy-mount.ts:59); the one that lacks it is the park observer (`{ threshold: 0 }`, renderers/GpuImagePane.tsx:1161-1178).
findings.proposal: Add a `"pending"`/`"unmounted"` status (or a `mounted: boolean` on Pane) and say precisely which Pane operations are legal before first mount; define `screenshot()` on a never-mounted pane as "force-mount, render, unmount" rather than "restore". Fix PERF-8 to name the GpuImagePane park observer, and state whether `mode: "stub"` and `MountOptions` can force eager mounting for host tests (today the escape hatches are a URL param and a `window` flag, lazy-mount.ts:21-55 — neither is reachable from `MountOptions`).

findings.claim: The per-kind typed map does not actually narrow at the entry points that return panes, so API-1 is unfixed in practice; and the closed `PaneKind` union cannot admit a `cairn-plot/extend` renderer, which makes §5's "settings SHAPES are stable-tier even in experimental modules" unimplementable for custom panes.
findings.evidence: §6.3 declares `Pane<K extends PaneKind = PaneKind>` but §6.2's accessors are untyped in K: `readonly panes: readonly Pane[]` and `pane(key: string): Pane`. With the default `K = PaneKind`, `getSettings(): PaneSettings[PaneKind]` is a union again and `setSettings(patch: Partial<PaneSettings[PaneKind]>)` — a parameter in contravariant position — accepts only the keys common to every kind, so `m.pane("render").setSettings({exposureEV: 2})` is a type error unless the host casts, which is exactly the bare-union ergonomics API-1 was raised against. Separately, §6.9's `registerRenderer(name, …, {settingsAdapter})` introduces a pane kind at runtime that cannot exist in the compile-time `PaneKind` union or in `enumerateOptions(kind, …)`'s registry projection (§6.7).
findings.proposal: Give the kind-carrying accessors a type argument with a runtime check (`m.pane<"image">("render")`, or `pane.as("image")` returning `Pane<"image">` and throwing on mismatch), and make `PaneKind`/`PaneSettings` open via declaration merging so `extend` can augment them. Then restate what "stable-tier shapes" means for a third-party-declared shape — cairn-plot cannot run a deprecation cycle for a shape it does not own.

findings.claim: §6.2/M0d's "content-derived resolve keys" cannot be derived for JS-authored data: the runtime hash is deliberately NOT content-addressed, so every re-authored handle produces fresh keys — update() never re-uses a cached resolution and both page-global stores grow without bound.
findings.evidence: `mintRuntimeHash()` is documented as "Uniqueness — not content-addressing … a fresh id per registration" (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/runtime-store.ts:117-126). The builder mints one per call for BOTH float and bytes inputs (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/builder/data.ts:103 and :213) — even for the identical `Float32Array` instance. The spec's own key recipe is "dataspec hash / runtime hash / src ref + selection suffix" (spec §6.2). Failing scenario: the M1 Tier-1 live loop (`cairnPlot.image(f32,{shape}); m.update(h2)` at ~1 Hz) mints hash N+1 each tick → new resolve key → full re-decode/re-upload every frame, plus one永 permanent entry in the append-only `cache` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/resolve-cache.ts:41,82-101) and one in `window.__cairnPlotRuntimeStore` (runtime-store.ts:53-70) per tick. The converse case is equally broken: for a stable `{url}`/store-hash spec the content key never changes, and the resolve cache has no invalidation, so a Tier-1 update() with genuinely new bytes behind the same URL shows the old frame forever (the RefStore that fixes this is M2). Today's object-identity keying accidentally gets this right in both directions.
findings.proposal: Don't claim content-derivation as a free M0 refactor. Specify ref naming the way §6.5 already does for adapters: (a) an optional author-supplied `contentKey` on every builder data input (and require it for live loops), (b) a WeakMap-on-buffer identity fallback for repeated same-instance authoring, (c) an explicit statement that url/hash refs are NOT self-invalidating until the M2 RefStore, so M1's Tier-1 story must be restricted to refs whose key the author names. Add a hashing-cost note (MB-scale float buffers cannot be digested synchronously in the builder).

findings.claim: §6.2's update() hold discipline ("previous frame until the new payload resolves — never a loading flash") is unimplementable on top of content-derived keys without a new key dimension: the existing hold is gated on base-key EQUALITY precisely so a key change must flash, and that behavior is pinned by the browser harness.
findings.evidence: The hold is `lastReadyRef.current?.base === baseKey` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-node.tsx:391-399), with the comment at :386-390 stating the gate exists so "a STACKED-slot flip changes the base key, so the flip-commit ruling ('a cold flip renders loading, never a hold of the previous slot's frame' — the stale-diff guarantee) is untouched". Cold key change → `placeholderMounts++` and a "Loading…" commit (plot-node.tsx:558-560). Both sides are harness-pinned: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/stack/stacked-diff-flip-resolve.browser.ts:175 asserts `placeholderMounts === 0` across warm flips, and /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/__tests__/enlarge-channel.browser.ts:137-157 asserts no placeholder during a channel pick. Failing scenario: after M0d, `m.update(h2)` with new pixels at pane key "render" changes the base content key — indistinguishable from a stacked flip to a different slot — so either update() flashes "Loading…" (violates §6.2) or the gate is loosened and a stacked flip holds the outgoing slot's frame (violates the stale-diff ruling the two harnesses pin). Diff panes are worse: the `|diffpair` key rides `synthDiffLeafOf`'s WeakMap on the compare NODE object (plot-node.tsx:837-862, used at :1334-1338 and :1640), so a re-authored descriptor invalidates the warm prefetch key too.
findings.proposal: Add an explicit identity dimension to §6.2: resolve keys become (paneKey, generation, contentKey) or the hold policy becomes an input ("hold" for same-pane-key content swaps, "flash" for slot flips), and state that the stacked prefetch + `synthDiffLeafOf` must compute the same content key through one shared helper. List "re-key the stacked/diff prefetch path and re-baseline the flip harnesses" as M0d work rather than asserting "content keys subsume object-identity keys".

findings.claim: M0a has no answer for who owns the per-pane layer registry: there are three independent, React-local minting sites for a pane's local layer id, and the enlarge/compare stage rebuilds a pane as a DIFFERENT instance with a different local layer — so a host's pushed layer and gestureSink silently disappear the moment the user enlarges.
findings.evidence: Site 1, the in-page pane: `useViewportSettings(pushSettingsLayer([`vp-st-${paneId}`], groups?.settingsGroupId))` with `paneId` minted inside the component (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-node.tsx:937,1037-1039). Site 2, the stage cell: a FRESH `PlotNodeView` subtree whose local layer is `vp-st-stage-${useId()}` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-selection-stage.tsx:376-381) — it re-renders the pane from the registered node, not the original pane instance. Site 3, a bare-mounted pane: `useViewportSettings([`vp-st-pane-${ownStoreId}`])` used when nothing is threaded (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/GpuImagePane.tsx:562-566; same in CpuImagePane.tsx:435-437 and :1116-1118). Failing scenario: host calls `pane.pushLayer(L,{gestureSink:true})` on pane "render", user selects two panes and hits enlarge; the stage cell resolves through `vp-st-stage-<id>` + selection/stage groups, none of which contain L — the host's values vanish from the enlarged view and every user tweak in the stage lands in the stage transient, never in L. MountOptions offers only `enlarge:"overlay"|"disabled"` (spec §6.2), i.e. the only host workaround is disabling enlarge.
findings.proposal: Specify a pane-key-addressed layer registry that lives OUTSIDE React (owned by the mount, created before/independent of component mount), and require all three sites to ADOPT the registry's layer ids rather than mint their own — including the stage cell adopting the source pane's key. Add a §6.4 ruling for what a stage cell inherits (host tier: yes; local tier: ?) and list "stage-cell layer adoption" and "remove the bare-pane own-store fallback (or key it by pane key)" as explicit M0a work.

findings.claim: M0b's write routing has to retrofit an origin/tier decision onto ~20 call sites that today share ONE untagged `set`, and the anchor formation seed — a programmatic write that goes through the same path — would be classified as a gesture and permanently commit the anchor's whole snapshot into the host's gestureSink layer on every selection formation.
findings.evidence: There is exactly one write path: `publishToSettingsStack` → top layer (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:183-190), exposed as `vst.set` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:92-99). It is consumed untagged by menus/gestures (plot-node.tsx:260-267 channel pick; GpuImagePane.tsx:622 kernel; CpuImagePane.tsx:490,1232 `publishSettings`), by the compare control (plot-node.tsx:1637), by the compositor (media-compare/compositor.tsx:916) — and by the ANCHOR FORMATION SEED, which calls the identical `set` with the pane's full effective snapshot (use-synced-image-settings.ts:112-128, `setRef.current?.(snapshotRef.current())`). Failing scenario: host pushes a shared layer L with `gestureSink:true` across a card grid; the user shift-clicks two panes; formation fires the seed; under §6.4 routing ("user gestures → topmost transient if one is live, else the gestureSink") the seed races the transient's existence — if it lands before/without the episode layer it writes the anchor's ENTIRE settings snapshot (exposure, encoding, colorMin/Max, channelSelect…) into L, which is shared by every other card and is persistent by construction. The same ambiguity applies to HOME (§6.4 already flags it as OPEN RULING §13.1).
findings.proposal: Make origin an explicit parameter of the write API in M0b (`set(patch, {origin})`), enumerate the current call sites that must be tagged non-gesture (formation seed, mirrored/sync applies, decode-failure revert at plot-node.tsx:351-355), and state that the seed writes the transient tier only — never the gesture sink. Size M0b as "~20 call-site edits across GpuImagePane/CpuImagePane/compositor/plot-node", not a routing tweak.

findings.claim: M0e understates the identity rewrite: pane identity today is a mount-order counter minted inside the component, and grid children are rendered with positional React keys — so any update() that inserts/removes/reorders a child remounts every following pane and loses exactly the things §6.2 promises to keep (settings, selection membership, GPU resources).
findings.evidence: Grid children: `children.map((child, i) => <PlotNodeView key={i} node={child} />)` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-node.tsx:1245). Pane identity: `const [paneId] = useState(nextSelectionPaneId)` (plot-node.tsx:937) over a process-wide counter (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/selection-store.ts:337-343), and that id is simultaneously the settings-layer id (`vp-st-${paneId}`, plot-node.tsx:1038), the selection-store membership id (:996,1058), and the stage registry key (`registerSelectionPane({paneId,…})`, :979-990). Failing scenario: `update()` prepends a new leaf to a 3-cell grid; React reconciles by index, every existing pane's component remounts, `nextSelectionPaneId` mints fresh ids, `vp-st-<new id>` is an EMPTY layer → all local settings reset, selection drops the panes (`store.remove` on unmount, :994-997), and the GPU pane is disposed and re-uploaded. Additional constraint the spec misses: pane keys are only "unique among siblings" (§6.1) while paneIds must be unique page-wide across independent React roots (selection-store.ts:299-336 explains why `useId` was rejected) — so M0e must mint (mountId + key path) composites and thread them through four consumers at once, touching the pinned page-wide-selection/selection-stage harnesses.
findings.proposal: Spell out in M0e: (1) author key → React `key` at every container render site (GridView, stacked slot, stage grid); (2) paneId becomes `${mountId}/${keyPath}` and replaces the counter in the selection store, the stage registry, and the settings layer id; (3) name the harness files that must be re-baselined. Also state what happens to the positional fallback across update() — an unkeyed reorder silently swaps two panes' settings.

findings.claim: `Pane.getSettings()` and `Pane.status` cannot be implemented in M0 from the layer stack: the stack resolves to `null` until something is written, effective values (defaults, prop seeds, view state, renderer-local state) live inside the renderers and are never published upward, and status is computed locally in the leaf.
findings.evidence: `resolveSettingsStack` returns `null` while all layers are empty (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:212-224); the effective value is decided at RENDER by "store value > prop seed" inside each pane (GpuImagePane.tsx:550-566, `propColormap`/`propTonemap` from descriptor props). Renderer-local state that §6.3 promises to expose is component state with no outward channel: channel selection `useState<ChannelSelection|null>` (plot-node.tsx:246), enlarge `useState(false)` (:274), and zoom/pan lives in the viewport sync bus, not the settings store. `status` is a local const in LeafView (`"loading"|"error"|"ready"`, plot-node.tsx:407-408) that is never lifted. Failing scenario: host mounts a 30-card dashboard, awaits `ready()`, and calls `pane.getSettings()` on an offscreen pane (§6.2 says these are "fully functional Pane objects — settings and events work") — it gets `null`/an empty object rather than the authored tonemap/encoding, and `pane.status` has no producer at all; a host dashboard cannot tell "stale" from "current" (Goal 5).
findings.proposal: Add an M0 item: a per-kind "effective settings projection" each renderer publishes (defaults ⊕ props ⊕ resolved stack ⊕ view state) plus a status/error channel from LeafView to the mount registry — and state that until it exists, `getSettings()` returns only the layer-resolved subset. Alternatively narrow §6.3 to "resolved overrides only" and drop the view-state claim from M0.

findings.claim: Generation release (§7 "every acquire has a release", M0d runtime-store unregister) collides with the fact that the runtime store, the blob-URL cache and the resolve cache are page-global and — once keys are content-derived — shared BY CONSTRUCTION across mounts; the spec defines no refcounting, so the first unmount frees data a second live mount is still using, and the specced leak gate is unsatisfiable.
findings.evidence: Runtime store is `window.__cairnPlotRuntimeStore`, explicitly "a page-level registry … so multiple plots on one page share it" (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/runtime-store.ts:22-27,53-70); entries are merged by hash at mount time (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-bootstrap.tsx:92-104). `objectUrlCache` mints one `blob:` URL per hash and never revokes (runtime-store.ts:96-115). The resolve cache is a module-level Map with only a test-only clear (resolve-cache.ts:41,113-118); today its natural GC story is the `sourceKey` WeakMap on node objects (resolve-cache.ts:12-33) — which disappears the moment keys become content strings. Failing scenarios: (a) the same `PlotHandle` mounted into two elements (or two cards sharing an image ref) — mount A unmounts, unregisters the shared runtime hash, mount B's pane goes blank on its next resolve; (b) §7's gate "mount → update ×100 → unmount → assert stores empty" can never pass on a page with any other live mount or legacy plot, since the stores are page-global; (c) revoked/never-revoked blob URLs are unaddressed either way.
findings.proposal: Specify refcounted ownership: runtime entries and resolve-cache entries carry a refcount keyed by (mount, generation), release decrements, eviction happens at zero, and blob URLs are revoked at zero. Restate the leak gate as "per-mount refcounts return to zero / store size returns to its pre-mount baseline", not "stores empty". Add explicit handling for mounting one handle twice.

findings.claim: M0a/M0c change the shape of a registry that is a `globalThis` cross-bundle singleton explicitly designed to tolerate mixed-vintage bundles on one page — an older core/addon copy writes flat settings straight into `lastStates`, bypassing tiers, and identity-bearing layer objects (`removeLayer(layer)`, `layer.dispose()`) don't survive two module copies.
findings.evidence: The registry is anchored on `globalThis` because the module is bundled into BOTH `core.iife.js` and `gpu-image.iife.js` and the two copies must share one set of buses/snapshots (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:93-118), with `??=` chosen so "an older registry object [keeps] working if bundles of mixed vintage share a page" (:192-198). The addon copy publishes directly via `publishImageSettings(groupId, sourceId, patch)` (:132-143) — a flat write with no tier. §8/WIRE-8 explicitly anticipates mixed vintages (it only logs a warning). Failing scenario: a page with a new core (tiered `{set, cleared}` entries) and an old gpu-image addon (flat `ImageSyncSettings` writes) — the old addon's kernel/compare-mode publishes land as untiered values that the new merge either ignores or mis-tiers, and cross-copy `instanceof`/object-identity layer handles fail.
findings.proposal: Add a registry `version` field with an explicit migration/reject rule in §8, require layer handles to be plain data addressed by string id (no class identity across bundle copies), and state the minimum-vintage requirement for the tiered registry (or gate tiering behind a capability probe on the shared registry object).

findings.claim: Selection and reference PICKING have no usable public surface in v2. Selection is a page-wide, cross-mount store with an explicit REFERENCE pin and stage channel; v2 exposes only `MountedPlot.on("selectionChange", (keys: string[]))` — per-mount, with keys that are not unique across mounts, no read of current selection, no reference get/set, no programmatic select, no stage events.
findings.evidence: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/selection-store.ts:1-28 — "ONE page-wide selection set … a selection can span independent React roots (the gallery renders each plot as a separate mount), which a per-grid or per-root React context could never do"; panes register a process-unique id (`nextSelectionPaneId`, :341). The store owns the reference pin (`reference()` :117-124, `setReference(id)` :130) and a stage channel (`requestStage` :217, StageMode "enlarge"|"compare"), and selection is what threads the shared viewport- and settings-sync group ids. Spec §6.2 gives one event `on("selectionChange", cb: (keys: string[]) => void)` on MountedPlot; §6.1 says keys are "unique among siblings" and §6.3 keys settings by "(mount id, pane key)" — so two cards mounted separately can both emit key "render" and the host cannot tell them apart. In cairn-track every card is its own mount, so the entire cross-card selection→reference→compare-stage flow (the orange REF pin, `REFERENCE_COLOR` :43) becomes unaddressable. `MountOptions.selection?: boolean` (§6.2) describes it as a per-mount page-wide toggle and never states that selection identity is shared across mounts.
findings.proposal: Promote selection to a page-level singleton in the public API: `getPlotSelection()` returning `{ getSelected(): PaneRef[], getReference(): PaneRef|null, setReference(ref), select(refs, mode), on("change"|"stageRequest", cb) }`, where `PaneRef` is the opaque `Pane` object (or `{mountId, key}`), not a bare string. Keep `MountedPlot.on("selectionChange")` as a filtered convenience view over it, and document `MountOptions.selection` as participation in (not creation of) that shared space.

findings.claim: A pane cannot be a host-defined drag SOURCE. The one shared drag-to-compare mechanic (image card + all four 3D cards) needs the host to write a host-specific payload into `dataTransfer` synchronously inside the pane's own dragstart; v2's `PaneInteraction` is an after-the-fact notification channel and cannot carry that.
findings.evidence: The pane's label chip is a host-driven drag source today: `ViewportPaneProps.isDraggable/onDragStart?: (e: React.DragEvent) => void` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/types.ts:281-282), consumed by every family — image (viewport/image-viewport.tsx:130-131, :172), mesh (:141,:203), pointcloud (:166,:206), boxes (:129,:201). The handler is host code that must run synchronously on the real event: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/SeriesChip.tsx:47-55 `startViewportDrag` sets `e.dataTransfer.setData(CAIRN_IMAGE_MIME, JSON.stringify(tag))`. 3D cards route the same payload through /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/MultiPaneGrid.tsx:68-74. The receiving side (card-kit/use-reference-drop.ts:64-86) distinguishes CAIRN_IMAGE_MIME (global reference) from CAIRN_SERIES_MIME (per-run reference) — i.e. the payload IS the reference-picking semantics. Spec §6.3 lists only `on("settings"|"status"|"interaction")`; an `interaction` callback receiving a serialized event object cannot mutate `dataTransfer`, and §6.2/§6.6 expose no DOM handler injection.
findings.proposal: Add a synchronous per-pane drag contract: either a descriptor/settings-level `dragPayload?: { label: string; items: Array<{mime: string; data: string}> }` resolved per pane (pure data, keeps the boundary), or a `MountOptions.onPaneDragStart(pane): DragPayload | null` callback invoked inside the library's dragstart. Also give the host a way to suppress it (`draggable: false`) so it does not fight host-level drags.

findings.claim: §6.7's enumerations are static per KIND, but every card's real menus are derived from the RESOLVED CONTENT of specific panes: overlay class lists, 3D property names, table columns, tensor dims — and compare-mode availability is gated per-pane by the actual resolved item/reference pair. v2 has no per-pane, content-derived option channel, so these menus cannot be built by a ported card.
findings.evidence: Overlay class toggles are aggregated from each pane's parsed artifact metadata, not from a registry: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/VisualContentCard.tsx:533-563 (`paneOverlays = paneMetadata.map(parseOverlay)`; classes collected from `ov.boxes[].class_id`, `ov.class_labels`, `m.class_labels`) and rendered as per-class buttons at :1215-1245 (swatch color from `overlayClassColor(classId)`). 3D property menus: MeshVisualCard.tsx:435 `propertyNames(item?.arrays.properties)` fed to PropertySelector (:445), plus `resolveActiveProperty(...)` at :128/:276/:345. Table column hiding needs the fetched table's column list; TensorCard.tsx:164-206 derives ndim/leadingDims/shapeLabel from the fetched meta. Content-dependent ENABLEMENT: VisualContentCard.tsx:1117-1119 renders native diff options disabled with the reason "Native diff is same-type only — not available for a cross-type reference" via `nm.enabledFor(viewData.items[0], viewData.referenceItems[0])`. Spec §6.7 offers only `enumerateOptions(kind, field)` and `getPaneCapabilities(kind)` — both keyed by kind, both static projections of internal registries.
findings.proposal: Add per-pane, content-derived facets: `pane.getFacets(): Record<string, OptionDescriptor[]>` (each option carrying `{id, label, enabled, disabledReason, swatch?}`) plus `pane.on("facets", cb)` firing when resolution changes, and move capability queries onto the Pane (`pane.getCapabilities()`) so `enabledFor`-style gating is expressible. Keep `enumerateOptions(kind, field)` for the genuinely static enums (colormaps, tonemaps).

findings.claim: Cross-pane derived data has no channel: hosts compute table diffs and figure merges from N panes' resolved payloads and push per-cell results BACK into panes. v2 gives no way to read a resolved payload/metadata back out, no way to push bulk per-cell annotations in, and §11 privatizes exactly the pure helpers (`computeTableDiff`, `mergeFigures`/`checkFigureMergeable`) with no public replacement.
findings.evidence: Table diff between runs: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/TableCard.tsx:329-345 fetches every pane's blob, calls `computeTableDiff(diffTables)` (imported from `@cairn-plot/lib/cairn-plot/table-diff`, :31-35) and hands each pane a `CellComparison[][]` via `diffStatuses={paneDiffStatuses[i]}` (:415-419) — an O(rows×cols) per-cell payload, not a settings value. Figure merge: FigureInteractiveCard.tsx:359-386 calls `checkFigureMergeable(...)`/`mergeFigures(...)` on N fetched Plotly figures and surfaces `figureMergeCheck.reason` in the UI (:656-658). Reference metadata: VisualContentCard.tsx:686-712 needs "the resolved reference's OWN metadata per pane (WS-VC4) — a 3D module's reference blob needs its own point-count/channels/bounds", passed on at :800-804. TensorCard.tsx:88-101/:190-197 slices the raw array host-side. Under §6.5 those payloads live in cairn-plot's RefStore; §6.3/§6.5 expose no `pane.getResolved()`, and §11 keeps table-diff internals private while §5's public entry list contains no computation helpers.
findings.proposal: Add `pane.getResolved(): { contentKey: string; payload: DataPayload; metadata?: unknown } | null` + `pane.on("resolved", cb)` so hosts compute over what the library already fetched; and either (a) keep `computeTableDiff`/`mergeFigures`/`checkFigureMergeable` in the stable `cairn-plot` entry as pure functions, or (b) express them as descriptor node kinds (`tableCompare`, `figureOverlay`) that take N refs and carry the annotation internally — and say which, since §11 currently forecloses (a) without providing (b).

findings.claim: The chart / figure / table / histogram kinds have no settings model and no milestone that creates one — yet §6.3 promises view state inside `PaneSettings` and M1 picks ScalarPlotCard as the first migration. §2 already admits "only the image family has a settings store" and M3 only covers 3D; M4 lumps Table/Figure/Histogram/ParallelCoords in with zero enabling work.
findings.evidence: ScalarPlot's entire state is props with host-owned callbacks, not a store: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/ScalarPlot.tsx:36-55 (`viewport`/`onViewportChange`, `promotedSeries`/`onPromotedSeriesChange`, `xScale`, `yScale`, `xRange`, `lineType`, `showLegend`, `selectedSeriesKeys`/`onSeriesClick`), and per-series show/hide is component-internal, unpersisted (`useSeriesVisibility`, :78-80). The host persists all of it: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/ScalarPlotCard.tsx:53-86, :540-547. Figure view state is a third, unmodelled family: FigureInteractiveCard.tsx:411-422 (`sharedView: SharedView`, merged from every pane's Plotly relayout) applied at :522/:578/:594. Series transforms are also host-side today — ScalarPlotCard.tsx:191-193 (`emaSmooth`, `filterOutliers`, `strideDownsample`), with the raw ghost taken from `emaSmooth`'s `{smoothed, raw}` and an EMA badge at :583-590 — while §11 privatizes "series utils" and no chart settings key exists to move smoothing into. So M1's stated proof ("settings round-trip") is being run on the one card whose settings kind does not exist.
findings.proposal: Add an explicit M0/M1 item: define and implement `PaneSettings["chart"]` (viewport, x/y scale + range, lineType, legend/series visibility, promoted axes, smoothing/outlier/downsample) and `PaneSettings["figure"]` (SharedView) and `PaneSettings["table"]` (rowsPerPage, hiddenColumns, diff mode), with the same store/sync machinery images have; rule explicitly whether smoothing is a plot setting (library-applied) or host preprocessing (and if the latter, keep the transform helpers public). Otherwise reorder M1 to a kind that exists.

findings.claim: v2's new layer masking model (`{set, cleared}` over top-level keys) cannot express the per-entity settings the cards actually have: per-series promotion, per-class overlay visibility, per-column hiding. Map-valued keys can only be replaced wholesale, so two host layers cannot contribute partial maps and `clear` cannot target one entry.
findings.evidence: Per-series: `promotedSeries: Record<string, PromotedSeriesConfig>` keyed by series key (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/ScalarPlot.tsx:45-48; host mirror ScalarPlotCard.tsx:60/:545-547) — with `onSeriesClick(seriesKey)` (:50-51) implying sub-pane addressing on the event side too. Per-class: `overlay.hiddenClasses: number[]` toggled one id at a time (VisualContentCard.tsx:571-575, :1221-1245). Per-column: TableCard `hiddenColumns` (:383-385). Spec §6.4 defines layer contents as `{ set: {...values}, cleared: [...keys] }` with `clear(keys)`/`unset(keys)` and a per-key tier resolution; a nested map value therefore resolves atomically from whichever tier wins, so a host layer that wants to hide class 3 has to copy the whole array from the tier below it — which defeats the sharing/masking model and races with gesture writes into a different tier.
findings.proposal: Define merge semantics for map/array-valued settings keys: either (a) declare such keys as "entry-addressable" with path-form operations (`layer.set({"overlay.hiddenClasses.3": true})`, `layer.clear(["promotedSeries.<key>"])`) and per-entry tier resolution, or (b) explicitly document them as atomic-replace and give the host a read of the resolved lower-tier value it must copy. Silence here makes every multi-layer card wrong in a subtle way.

findings.claim: `update()` has no ordering, coalescing, or abort contract, yet the step slider — present on every artifact card — fires one full re-author per tick with all-new data refs. Overlapping updates can land out of order and leave the pane showing a step the slider is no longer on.
findings.evidence: Every slider tick changes the step and hence every pane's data ref: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/use-step-slider.ts:49-55 (`onSliderChange` → `setIdx` + `updateSettings({sliderStep})`, `currentStep = globalSteps[safeIdx]`), driven by StepSlider's range input; `currentStep` then feeds artifact resolution for every pane and for the reference (card-kit/use-media-reference.ts:133-164; TableCard.tsx:321-325; VisualContentCard.tsx:986-990). Spec §6.2 defines `update(next): Promise<void>` with a hold discipline ("previous frame until the new payload resolves") but no latest-wins rule, no in-flight abort, and no statement about concurrent calls; §6.5's coalescing ("coalesced latest-wins per ref, in-flight aborted via the signal") is scoped to RefStore invalidation, i.e. Tier-2 only — and M1 explicitly migrates ScalarPlotCard on Tier-1 `update()`. Failing scenario: drag the slider from step 10 to step 40; update(step 10) hits a cold artifact and resolves after update(step 40)'s cached one; the last write into the pane's swap chain is step 10 while the slider reads 40.
findings.proposal: Specify `update()` as latest-wins per mount: a superseded call aborts its in-flight resolutions and its promise settles with a documented outcome (`{superseded: true}` or resolve-as-noop); guarantee the last-authored handle is the one that lands. Add a note that `status: "stale"` covers the hold window, and give hosts a `m.updateSettled()` / generation counter for tests.

findings.claim: `ScreenshotOpts` is referenced three times and never defined, and the real card "screenshot" is not a canvas readback at all — it is a composed export (grid layout, per-pane labels, REF/prediction grouping, a colorbar drawn from the actual 256×3 colormap LUT). §6.7's "ids + labels + flags only, no internals" removes the LUT and palette accessors the host needs with no replacement.
findings.evidence: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/VisualContentCard.tsx:977-1013: `handleScreenshot` builds `CompositePane[]` with `{label, groupWithNext, skipColormap}` for REF/pred pairs and passes `colorbar: { lut: getColormapLUT(cmap), name, diverging: DIVERGING_COLORMAPS.has(cmap) }` plus a column count into `exportImagesAsComposite`. That exporter consumes the raw LUT: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/lib/download.ts:110-121 ("{ lut: 256×3 Uint8Array, name }"), :159-170 and :267-289. The host also needs palette data outside panes: `DIVERGING_COLORMAPS` for a settings hint (components/viewport-registry.tsx:237-242) and `SERIES_COLORS` for its own chip strip (components/SeriesChipStrip.tsx:1, :60/:101; ScalarPlotCard.tsx:199; BarChartCard.tsx:119). Spec §6.2/§6.3/§7 mention `screenshot(opts?: ScreenshotOpts)` without ever defining the type, and §7 only promises per-pane readbacks composed for a whole mount.
findings.proposal: Define `ScreenshotOpts` (at minimum: `scale` or `native: true` to render at content resolution rather than on-screen size, `background`, `includeOverlays`, `labels`, `layout: {cols}`, `colorbar`), and either ship the composite exporter as public API or extend §6.7's data projections with `getColormapLUT(id): Uint8Array`, `isDiverging(id)`, and the categorical `seriesPalette()` — palette data is data, not internals.

findings.claim: §6.2's "content-derived resolve keys" has no derivable content identity for JS-authored (runtime-store) data — the exact path every cairn-track card uses — so the stated payoff ("an updated handle whose leaf data is unchanged re-uses the cached resolution and GPU upload") is unimplementable as written, and both plausible implementations are wrong.
findings.evidence: Spec §6.2 lists the key as "dataspec hash / runtime hash / src ref + selection suffix". But the runtime hash is explicitly NOT content-addressed: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/runtime-store.ts:117-126 — `mintRuntimeHash()` returns `runtime:<n>-<rand>` with the comment "Uniqueness — not content-addressing — is all that's needed". It is minted fresh per builder call: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/builder/data.ts:103 (float path) and :213 (bytes path). So `cairnPlot.image(sameFloat32Array, …)` re-authored for `m.update(h2)` yields a NEW hash ⇒ new content key ⇒ guaranteed cache miss, re-decode and re-upload of every leaf on every update, and §7's generation release then frees the still-valid GPU texture. The obvious repair — keying off the buffer OBJECT (a WeakMap) — reintroduces exactly the object identity §6.2 is abandoning AND breaks the common live-dashboard idiom of writing new pixels into one reused Float32Array: same key, pane never updates. Hashing an 8MP f32 buffer per frame is the third, unaffordable branch. §6.5's Tier 2 gets this right (`DataResult.contentKey`, "the adapter names the content ... cairn-plot never guesses (LD7)"); Tier 1 gets no equivalent.
findings.proposal: Apply LD7 to the authoring boundary too: add an explicit `dataKey?: string` (or `version`) to the builder data options and make it the runtime leg of the content key; default to mint-per-call and DOCUMENT that omitting it means "treated as new content on every update" (correct, cold). State the aliasing rule outright — buffers handed to the builder are owned/immutable, mutate-in-place is undefined unless `dataKey` changes — and add a reconcile harness case (M0 gates) asserting that re-authoring with an unchanged `dataKey` performs zero re-upload while a changed one does.

findings.claim: §6.7's `enumerateOptions(kind, field)` / `getPaneCapabilities(kind)` are specified as synchronous, static, per-kind projections on the stable `cairn-plot` entry, but the registries they project live in a capability-gated, asynchronously-loaded addon chunk. The functions cannot be static, cannot be keyed by kind alone, and cannot be exported from core without breaking a documented bundle invariant.
findings.evidence: The diff-kernel registry is a module-local Map inside engine/**: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/engine/kernels/kernel-registry.ts:136-151. engine/** is fenced OUT of core by contract: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/vite.plot-gpu-image.config.ts:14-22 — "BUNDLE-GUARD INVARIANT … the engine … must be reachable ONLY from this addon chunk, never from core.iife.js". The only consumer of `listDiffMenuModes` is the addon entry (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-gpu-image-addon.tsx:60), whose registration is gated on an async `getSharedDevice()` and on `window.__cairnPlotUseGpuImage` (:44-56) — i.e. the true answer depends on WebGPU availability (which is itself secure-context gated) and on chunk load order, and settles AFTER mount. A host card header calling `enumerateOptions("compare","kernel")` at render time gets an empty or wrong menu on a plain-HTTP page, on a no-WebGPU browser, or simply too early — and there is no ready/subscribe/availability channel anywhere in §6.7. Two further hazards the spec never names: (a) these registries are module-local, not globalThis-anchored, and /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:93-118 documents in detail how that same pattern silently produced two disjoint registries across the core/addon split — the identity of "the internal registry" a projection reads is undefined; (b) §5's entry-point table doesn't mention the core/addon chunk model at all, so there is no place the spec can even say which entry a projection lives in.
findings.proposal: Re-scope enumeration to the mount/pane (`m.capabilities(kind)` / `pane.capabilities()`), make it a snapshot plus a `on("capabilities")` change event, and have every OptionDescriptor carry `available: boolean` + `unavailableReason` (e.g. "no WebGPU") so host chrome can render a disabled entry instead of a broken one. Add a §5 subsection declaring the chunk model (core / gpu-image / figure / three) and, per registry, whether it is core-resident or addon-resident; require any addon-resident registry consulted from the public API to be globalThis-anchored the way the settings bus already is.

findings.claim: §6.7's "The ids are the same ids the settings accept (one vocabulary)" is false against the code: compare kernels already ship TWO vocabularies (public short names vs registry ids) that the builder maps between, and they have already drifted. §8's alias rule covers removals, not this dual-namespace split — a host menu built from enumerateOptions will not round-trip through the builder.
findings.evidence: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/builder/validate.ts:38-50 — `COMPARE_KERNEL_MODES` maps public `compare(mode=)` names to registry kernel ids (`abs`→`absolute`, `rel_signed`→`relative_signed`, `square`→`squared`). The split is enshrined cross-language as two separate contract entries: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/schema/cairn-plot-contracts.json keys `compareKernelPublicNames` AND `compareKernelModes`. The settings side carries the REGISTRY id: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:72-73 — "Selected diff kernel id (e.g. \"absolute\"/\"hdr-flip\"/\"ssim\")" — and `hdr-flip` isn't in the public table at all (which has `flip`/`flip_ldr`), so the two vocabularies have already drifted. Meanwhile the spec's own §6.1 example authors with the PUBLIC name (`kernel: "flip"`) while §6.3 says settings and enumeration share one id space. Secondary defect in the same surface: OptionDescriptor labels come from hardcoded English `label` fields on the registry entries (kernel-registry.ts KernelMetaBase.label; image/encodings/registry.ts:184 `DisplayEncoding.label`), and §6.7 gives hosts no locale argument and no label-override hook, so cairn-track cannot localize chrome it is now expected to own.
findings.proposal: Name ONE public vocabulary in §6.7 (the contract public names are the better candidate — they are already cross-language) and specify the ingest mapping as a documented table under §8 alongside the alias rule, with `migrateSettings` normalizing legacy registry ids. Add a contract guard (contracts.test.ts sibling) asserting `enumerateOptions(kind, field)` ids ⊆ ids the builder validator and the settings ingest both accept, per field. Extend OptionDescriptor to `{id, label, labelKey}` and let a host pass a label override map, so labels are data rather than baked English.

findings.claim: Pane-key uniqueness is specified at sibling scope but consumed at mount scope, and `selectionChange` reports bare keys from a selection set that is deliberately page-wide and cross-mount — so both the addressing and the event payload are ambiguous by construction.
findings.evidence: §6.1: "Keys are unique among siblings." §6.3: `pane(key: string): Pane; // throws on unknown key`, settings keyed by "(mount id, pane key)", and §6.2 makes update() correspondence key-based mount-wide. A nested `cairnPlot.grid([grid([image({key:"render"})]), grid([image({key:"render"})])])` is legal under the stated rule and makes `pane("render")`, the settings registry, and update() correspondence all ambiguous. On selection: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/selection-store.ts:1-30 and :299-319 make selection ONE document-scoped store shared across independent React roots by design (`GLOBAL_SELECTION_BASE`), with per-episode group ids derived from a single `base` (:279-297). So `m.on("selectionChange", cb: (keys: string[]) => void)` can be fired for a selection containing panes belonging to a different mount — or to a different host application on the same page — and those keys are meaningless in the receiver's namespace and may collide with its own. §6.2's MountOptions comment says "Scope/disable page-global features" but only offers `selection?: boolean`, i.e. disable; there is no scoping, even though `paneSyncGroups(store, paneId, base)` is already parameterized by `base` and could support one.
findings.proposal: Require keys unique per MOUNT (validate at build/mount with a clear error naming both offenders) or make the public address a path (`"grid.0/render"`) and say so. Change the event to `on("selectionChange", (panes: Pane[], info: { foreignPanes: number }) => void)` so cross-mount members are representable, and turn the option into `selection?: "page" | "mount" | false` with a per-scope selection store instance (the `base` parameter already exists).

findings.claim: The three-tier write routing is correct but unobservable: `setSettings` writes to the BOTTOM tier, so any host layer or live transient silently shadows it — and because `getSettings()` returns only resolved values and `on("settings")` fires only on resolved-value change, a shadowed host write produces no value change and no event. The host cannot distinguish "applied" from "swallowed".
findings.evidence: §6.4 fixes the order `[local, ...host layers, ...transients]` and routes `pane.setSettings(patch)` to local. Merge is later-wins: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:212-224 (`Object.assign({}, ...layers)`), and the pane-local layer is already the bottom of the real stack: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-node.tsx:1038 (`pushSettingsLayer([`vp-st-${paneId}`], groups?.settingsGroupId)`). Concrete failure: a card pushes a shared host layer with `{encoding:"turbo"}` (the normal §6.6 `<Plot layers={[hostLayer]}>` case), then a code path calls `pane.setSettings({encoding:"magma"})`. Nothing renders differently, `getSettings().encoding` still reads `"turbo"`, and §6.4's echo rule ("fires once per resolved-value change") means no `settings` event fires. A React host that binds a `<select>` to `getSettings()` sees its own selection snap back with no diagnostic. The same trap applies during any live selection episode, which is precisely when a user is most likely to be driving host chrome.
findings.proposal: Add tier introspection to §6.3: `getSettings({ tier })` and a `sources: Record<key, "local"|"host"|"transient"|"default">` map on the settings snapshot, so a host control can render the winning tier. Specify that `setSettings` on a currently-shadowed key emits a dev-mode warning naming the shadowing tier, and re-document `setSettings` as "seed the pane's local/default tier" — with the guidance that host chrome intended to WIN should write its own `gestureSink` layer instead.

findings.claim: Content-derived resolve keys make the existing permanent-error caching strictly worse, and the recovery mechanisms the spec adds (`m.refresh(ref?)`, retry-on-invalidation) exist only in Tier 2 / M2 — so the M1 milestone ships a design in which one transient failure bricks a leaf for the life of the page, with no documented path out of `status: "error"`/`"stale"`.
findings.evidence: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/resolve-cache.ts:82-101 — on rejection the entry keeps its rejected `promise`; every later `resolveCached(key, …)` hits line 85 (`if (existing?.promise) return existing.promise.then(...)`) and re-yields the SAME rejection, so `run` never re-executes. §2 acknowledges "errors cached forever", but §6.2/M0d only add content-derivation plus release hooks; §6.5's error policy ("retries on the NEXT invalidation or an explicit `m.refresh(ref?)`") is explicitly RefStore/Tier-2, i.e. M2. Under §6.2's new keying this gets worse: because keys are now content-derived, re-authoring the identical handle after a failed fetch produces the SAME key and therefore replays the cached rejection deterministically — under today's object-identity keys a freshly-built descriptor node at least got a new key and retried. §6.3 introduces `status: "error"|"stale"` as states a dashboard "must render" without ever specifying the transition back to `ready`.
findings.proposal: Spec the resolve-cache error policy in §6.2/M0d: do not cache rejections (or cache them with a retry token that `update()`/refresh clears), and add eviction of errored entries on generation release. Make `m.refresh(ref?)` tier-agnostic and add `pane.retry()`. Include an explicit status transition table (loading→ready|error; ready→stale→ready|error) in §6.3, and add a harness case: fail a fetch, re-`update()` with the same handle, assert the pane recovers.

findings.claim: The lifecycle/observability surface is incomplete and internally inconsistent: §6.2 relies on a `paneRemoved` event that the API never declares, `MountedPlot` has no error channel at all (mount failure is currently swallowed into a DOM message), and the concurrency/teardown edge cases — update during update, unmount during ready(), retained Pane handles after their key disappears — are unspecified.
findings.evidence: §6.2 states "its settings are dropped after `paneRemoved` fires", but `MountedPlot.on` in §6.3 declares exactly one event: `on(ev: "selectionChange", ...)`. There is no paneAdded/paneRemoved/error/updated. Mount-level failures never reach a host today by explicit design: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-bootstrap.tsx:173-176 — "NEVER throws to the host — a descriptor read failure degrades to a visible message" — implemented at :194-217, so a `ready()` built on this resolves successfully on a plot that failed to load, and §6.3's `status` is per-pane only (there are no panes when the tree itself fails). Nothing states whether `update()` called while a previous `update()` is in flight is queued, superseded, or an error, nor what the earlier promise does; whether `unmount()` during a pending `ready()`/`update()`/`screenshot()` settles or hangs those promises; whether an `Unsub` is idempotent or auto-invalidated at unmount (the spec's own memory/leak gate in §7 asserts "stores empty" but says nothing about listener sets — cf. the plain listener Set at resolve-cache.ts:47-61); or what a Pane object the host still holds does after its key disappeared in an update().
findings.proposal: Add a §6.2 lifecycle subsection with a state machine (mounting→ready→updating→unmounted) and explicit rulings: `update()` is latest-wins, superseded promises resolve (not reject) and a final `updated` event carries the settled generation; `unmount()` rejects every pending promise with a named `PlotUnmounted` error; a detached Pane throws `PaneDetached` on every method; `Unsub` is idempotent and all listeners are dropped at unmount (asserted by the leak gate). Declare the full MountedPlot event union — `paneAdded`, `paneRemoved`, `error`, `updated`, `selectionChange` — and route the currently-swallowed descriptor/mount failure into `error` plus a rejected/observable `ready()`.

findings.claim: The v2 additions bring three more page-global mutable registration surfaces into the STABLE tier — `configureEngine` (§7), `registerDataSource` (§6.5), `registerRenderer` (§6.9) — with no scoping, no stated collision rule, and no trust boundary on the refs a descriptor may name. `configureEngine` in particular leaks current engine internals into a surface that requires a deprecation cycle to change.
findings.evidence: Budgets are module-level constants consumed inline in the eviction loops: /Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/engine/pool.ts:129 (`MAX_LIVE_SWAPCHAINS = 12`), :149 (`MAX_RETAINED_SOURCE_TEXTURES = 6`), used at :516 and :576. `configureEngine` therefore mutates page-global state inside the addon chunk (same bundle-guard problem as R2-2), and the LAST caller on the page wins for EVERY mount — directly against §6.2's embedded-use goal, where two independent cards must not be able to reconfigure each other's memory budget. The parameter names are also today's implementation vocabulary: `maxLiveSwapchains` is a WebGPU-surface term, and §7 simultaneously plans to move retention from texture-count to byte accounting as M-perf — i.e. the stable-tier signature is scheduled to change semantics before it has shipped. On registration collisions the codebase has no house rule to inherit: `registerEncoding` throws on a duplicate id (image/encodings/registry.ts:389-394) and `registerDiffKernel` throws (engine/kernels/kernel-registry.ts:138-142), while `registerRenderer` overwrites by name (plot-bootstrap.tsx:277) — and §6.5 defines `registerDataSource("track", …)` as a bare global scheme string with no ruling either way. Finally, refs are descriptor data, and descriptors legitimately arrive from a server (`mode:"endpoint"`, plot-bootstrap.tsx:149-156, plus the `?src=` fetch at :130-138), so a ref is externally-influenceable input handed to a host adapter that will typically attach the host's credentials — the spec says nothing about validating it or restricting which schemes a given mount may reference.
findings.proposal: Move budgets to `MountOptions.budgets` (per-mount, with a documented page-global default) and keep any true global knob in `cairn-plot/extend`, out of the stable tier, until byte accounting lands; name it in engine-neutral terms (`maxLivePanes`, `retainedBytes`). State the collision rule for every public registration function (recommend: throw on duplicate id, mirroring the two existing registries) and give `DisposableRegistration.dispose()` a defined behavior for in-flight `get`s. Add a short trust-boundary paragraph to §6.5: refs are opaque untrusted strings, cairn-plot performs no URL construction or joining on them, adapters MUST validate/allow-list before use, and a mount may declare the schemes its descriptor is permitted to reference.
